lede: The biggest thing to watch this week is a short but significant special meeting at Telluride Medical Center, where the board takes up a proposal to engage Jensen Partners for due diligence with CommonSpirit Health — one of the country's largest hospital systems — a step that could signal a major affiliation or transaction ahead for our local medical center. On the land-use side, a P&Z Chair hearing will consider merging two lots on West Columbia into a single 5,625-square-foot parcel in a Historic Residential zone, and Ouray City Council holds a public hearing on its 2027 budget with utility rate ordinances up for second reading. Closer to home, the Telluride Ecology Commission takes up a draft ordinance that would ban gas-powered lawn and garden equipment in town limits by 2028–2030.

notable.stake: Board votes on hiring due-diligence support for potential CommonSpirit Health affiliation.
P&Z Chair decides lot-line vacation merging two Historic Residential parcels on W Columbia.
Public hearing on Ouray's 2027 budget; utility rate ordinances on second reading for adoption.
Draft ordinance would ban gas-powered lawn equipment in Telluride by 2028–2030.
